barriers.description: Many recruited clients did not attend confirmed design sessions, reducing participant numbers available for co-design and usability testing. This diminished end-user involvement constrained iterative design activities.
barriers.justification: Participants' nonattendance directly hindered the designers' ability to facilitate user involvement, manage evolving user understanding, and run sufficient evaluation and iteration cycles (phases 2–4).
barriers.reference_excerpt: We intended to recruit 8 clients and members of their social networks in design rounds 2, 4, and 5. Approximately half of the recruited participants (n=9) did not show up at these design rounds (phases 2 and 3).

barriers.description: Designers were unable to recruit as many members of clients' social networks as intended, resulting in limited participation from this stakeholder group. This reduced diversity of input impeded exploration of social-network–related requirements and features.
barriers.justification: The limited involvement of social network members constrained designers' ability to understand those actors' contexts and needs, specify comprehensive user requirements, and iterate solutions addressing peer-related functionality.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Another limitation was the involvement of a limited number of members of women’s social networks in most rounds of intervention design. Identical to clients' no shows, we were not able to recruit as many members of social networks as intended.

barriers.description: The target population for recruitment was very small (fewer than 1% of births qualify for the program), limiting the available pool of end users for design activities. This made recruiting sufficient participants for iterative rounds challenging.
barriers.justification: A small eligible population reduced designers' capacity to manage user understanding and facilitate user involvement across multiple iterative sessions, constraining the robustness and generalizability of requirements gathering and testing.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Involving disadvantaged populations in research is challenging [5,53]. Moreover, with less than 1% of the births per Dutch municipality qualifying to enroll in VoorZorg, our target population is very small.

barriers.description: The prototype used for usability testing had limited functionality, which may have prevented detection of usability problems that would appear during free use. This limited maturity constrained the depth of evaluation possible in phase 4.
barriers.justification: Evaluating an early, functionally limited prototype restricted designers' ability to fully evaluate designs and integrate feedback from real-world use, thereby limiting iteration and refinement based on comprehensive usability insights.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Moreover, we evaluated the usability of a prototype with limited functionality. The think aloud method was based on certain real-life tasks that covered all the functionalities. This may have highlighted other usability problems that would have occurred during free use of the app. The limited functionality of the prototype may also have resulted in an incomplete insight into usability problems.
